- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is falling, model underestimates downward momentum; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price drops — if last 3 days show sharp decline, forecast should not drop below 5% below recent low.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with sentiment trend 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early period (first 5–7 days) — apply 3–5% downward correction to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.7) and price is flat or rising, model tends to overforecast — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
